extracted.intended_audience: journalists, media industry professionals, and readers interested in media ethics and technology
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and concerns for evaluating AI-scribed journalism, including originality, disclosure, editorial oversight, factual accuracy, and evidence for plagiarism claims. Focused on how publishers should produce and label AI-generated stories and how investigators establish copying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / No plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Futurism uncovered 'extensive evidence' that suggests the AI-generated articles are so close to work of competitors like Forbes that they constitute plagiarism; finding 'deep structural and phrasing similarities' and providing side-by-side examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators look for deep structural and phrasing similarities, not only verbatim copying. Anti-patterns include minor edits to sentence syntax, word choice, or structure that leave the underlying phrasing and organization intact. Publishers should ensure AI output is original and not a close paraphrase of existing work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Byline and authorship transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not mislabel AI-written pieces as written by 'staff' or otherwise present them as human-authored when they are AI-generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TheWrap notes CNET removed the word 'staff' from bylines of dozens of AI-generated stories after scrutiny. Best practice: clearly identify when content is AI-generated to avoid misleading readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of AI use and human editorial oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Pages featuring AI-generated articles included disclosures and CNET noted they were 'scrutinized by a human editor before being published.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers should provide clear disclosure that an article was produced with AI and describe the nature/extent of human review. Claims of human scrutiny should be backed by demonstrable fact-checking and editorial intervention, since disclosure alone does not guarantee accuracy or originality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factual accuracy and fact-checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Earlier Futurism reporting found AI-written content was 'riddled with factual errors.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Human editors must rigorously fact-check AI-generated copy; inadequate fact-checking is an anti-pattern and can leave published pieces inaccurate despite purported oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training data and provenance transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions remain about 'what data had been used to train the AI,' and CNET executives 'refused' to elaborate in a cited meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosing training sources or the provenance of data used to generate articles helps assess risks of copying and plagiarism. Lack of transparency on training data is a red flag for potential misuse of competitors' content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence standards for alleging plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Futurism provided side-by-side examples and described the bot parsing already-published articles and making adjustments — sometimes minor, sometimes major — to syntax, word choice, and structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To substantiate plagiarism claims, present side-by-side comparisons highlighting structural and phrasing parallels, show patterns (e.g., repeated transformations that preserve original meaning/order), and document specific instances where the AI output closely mirrors existing articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of paraphrase and composition (avoid 'Frankensentences')
rubrics_metrics.description: The process was described as mashing two sentences together, breaking one apart, assembling chunks into new 'Frankensentences,' and repeating until an entire article is produced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI-generated content should synthesize information coherently rather than mechanically recombining fragments from source material. Anti-patterns include awkwardly merged sentences, incoherent 'Frankensentences,' and formulaic stitch‑together prose that signals low-quality paraphrasing or direct reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper attribution and citation of sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The allegation centers on the bot directly plagiarizing work of competitors and human writers without appropriate acknowledgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When AI systems draw on publicly available reporting or other sources, publishers should ensure proper attribution, citations, or links to original reporting where appropriate. Failure to attribute source material increases risk of plagiarism allegations.
